currentContext.strengths: Century-strong TVS brand heritage and part of the TVS Mobility Group|End-to-end, integrated 'One TVS SCS' model bundling ISCS and IFM for tailored client solutions|Asset-light, tech-led operating model with AI and emerging Agentic AI adoption|Global network combined with strong domestic Indian presence across key trade corridors|Marquee customer base serving 100 Fortune 500 customers in FY26 (up from 91 in FY25)|Cost-efficient delivery through the Madurai Centre of Excellence|Strategic carrier partnerships enabling capacity procurement and service reliability in GFS
currentContext.strategies: The Company has a formal Dividend Distribution Policy setting out internal and external factors the Board weighs in determining pay-out. For FY26 the Directors decided not to recommend any dividend, choosing to conserve resources for future growth; no amount was transferred to reserves and no public deposits were accepted. Overall stance is reinvestment-led, prioritising internal capital for growth over distributions.|Persistent gender-diversity gap: women comprise only ~8% of total employees and workers, 20% of the Board of Directors, and 0% of Key Managerial Personnel.|High permanent-employee attrition: FY26 turnover rate for permanent employees was ~31% (33% female, 31% male), broadly in line with prior years.|Community and environmental initiatives under 'TVS SCS Cares': restored six village ponds improving safe water access for 5,000+ residents, planted 5,000 palm-tree saplings for green cover/biodiversity, ran a village medical camp serving 150+ villagers, and collected 108.71 kg of waste in a coastal clean-up drive.|Global CSR/volunteering programmes across geographies (Melbourne food-donation drive, North America hygiene/shelter donations, TVS SCS Europe 'Save the Children' fundraiser).|BRSR reporting boundary is standalone only, with no external assurance obtained for the reporting period — a limitation on the scope and independent verification of sustainability disclosures.|Sustainability approach positioned as anchored in transparency, accountability and continuous improvement, with a Remuneration and Diversity policy in place.
currentContext.expansion: TVS Supply Chain Solutions describes itself as a tech-led and asset-light supply chain solutions provider, so the FY26 report's routed sections disclose no plant/capacity capex projects with rupee outlays or commissioning timelines; expansion is organic and contract-led rather than fixed-asset-led. During FY26 the company re-organised its segment structure, unifying the erstwhile ISCS and Integrated Facility Management (IFM) capabilities into a single ISCS segment to deliver bundled, end-to-end services tailored to client needs, while Global Forwarding Solution (GFS) continues to house freight forwarding. Geographic and customer expansion came through strategic contract wins: a significant India contract with a leading global wind-turbine manufacturer, a European win with a leading multinational retail chain, and encircling/growth of North America operations with a leading global agricultural-equipment manufacturer. New business development added ~INR 1,206.74 crores of additional revenue in FY26, and the number of Fortune 500 customers serviced grew to 100 (from 91 in FY25). No forward financial guidance, buyback, or dividend policy statement appears in the routed sections.

risks.risk: Senior leadership churn at the top
risks.note: Rapid turnover in key managerial personnel — CEO appointed Jan 22, 2026, Managing Director Ravi Viswanathan resigned effective June 30, 2026, and Vikas Chadha appointed MD effective July 1, 2026 — creates continuity and execution risk at the helm of the business.

Growth is anchored to a relatively small base of large, sophisticated clients (100 Fortune 500 customers serviced, up from 91), and individual strategic contract wins (Global Wind Turbine maker, European retail chain, North America agri-equipment maker); loss or scaling-down of a major account would be material.

risks.risk: Dependence on continuous new business development
risks.note: The asset-light, tech-led model relies on winning fresh contracts each year to sustain the topline (FY26 added ~Rs 1,206.74 crores of new-business revenue); a slowdown in wins directly compresses growth.

risks.risk: Extensive foreign operations and FX / geopolitical exposure
risks.note: The consolidated group operates through a large web of international subsidiaries across the UK, USA, Germany, Spain, Singapore, Thailand, Korea, Malaysia, Vietnam, Mexico, Indonesia and others, exposing it to currency, cross-border regulatory and geopolitical risk even though standalone exports are Nil.

The segment structure was reorganised during FY26 to merge ISCS and IFM (formerly Rico Logistics) into a single unified ISCS model; combining acquired/foreign entities and re-bundling service lines carries integration and execution risk.

risks.risk: Margin volatility in the asset-light logistics model
risks.note: Profitability leans on cost-optimisation initiatives and operating leverage from new wins rather than owned assets, leaving margins sensitive to input costs, contract pricing and utilisation swings.

Demand is spread across Automotive, FMCG/FMCD, Electronics, E-commerce, Telecom & IT, Oil & Gas, Cement, Retail, Engineering & Capital Goods, Renewable Energy and Healthcare — a downturn in one or more of these cyclical industries flows through to supply-chain volumes.

one-line thesis: TVS SCS delivered a spectacular FY26 finish with Q4 revenue crossing Rs 3,000 cr (+21.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 80 bps to 7.3%, driven by a record Rs 524 cr in new business wins and a structural turnaround in Europe. The acquisition of Swamy & Sons and robust Rs 6,100 cr order pipeline position the company for sustained double-digit growth in FY27, shifting the narrative from recovery to accelerated expansion.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs 3,032 cr (Q4, +21.3% YoY), Rs 11,003 cr (FY26, +10.1% YoY). EBITDA: Rs 222 cr (Q4, +37.5% YoY), Margin 7.3% (+80 bps YoY); FY26 Adj EBITDA Rs 773 cr (+14.5%). PAT: Reported PBT Rs 25.7 cr (Q4) impacted by Rs 5.2 cr exceptional labor code cost; FY26 Reported PBT Rs 274.1 cr includes Rs 177.2 cr one-off IndIT gain in Q1; Adj PBT FY26 Rs 99.3 cr (+166% YoY). Order Book: Robust pipeline of Rs 6,100 cr. Net Debt: ~Rs 350-370 cr (mostly short-term WC). One-offs: Q1 IndIT gain (Rs 177.2 cr); Q4 Exceptional labor code cost (Rs 5.2 cr).
guidance: Revenue: Double-digit to early teen growth expected for FY27. Margin: ISCS target 9.5%-10%; GFS cautious due to rate volatility; Consolidated Adj EBITDA margin trajectory towards 7.3%-7.4% initially, medium-term aspiration 10.5%-11% (ISCS) and 6%-6.5% (GFS). Order Inflow: Targeting 12%-15% of prior year revenue as new wins (achieved 12.1% in FY26). Capex: Asset-light model; no significant fixed asset investment; focus on working capital and tech integration.
order book & pipeline: Rs 6,100 cr total pipeline; Q4 new wins Rs 523.7 cr (record high, 21% of Q4 FY25 revenue); Typical conversion ratio ~22%; Wins span EV, electrical equipment, home appliances, retail, IT services, and industrial automation.
segment / subsidiary detail: ISCS: Revenue Rs 2,283 cr (Q4, +17.5% YoY), EBITDA Rs 212.8 cr (9.3% margin vs 8.5% YoY); driven by Europe turnaround and India growth. GFS: Revenue Rs 748.8 cr (Q4, +34.8% YoY) led by India ocean freight volumes; EBITDA Rs 18.3 cr (2.4% margin vs 1.6% YoY); margins pressured by global freight rates despite volume growth.
growth verticals / optionality: Acquisition of Swamy & Sons 3PL (completed May 2026) for FMCG/consumption depth in India; MOU with ALA for Defense/Aerospace entry (high certification barriers); 'China Plus One' relocation trends benefiting India manufacturing clients; Cross-sell/upsell within 100 Fortune 500 clients (added 9 new in FY26).
margins & cost dynamics: ISCS margins improved via Europe recovery and operating leverage; GFS margins structurally lower but improved via cost optimization offsetting rate pressure; Employee costs up due to inflation/new projects but offset by 'Project One' cost takeouts; IndAS 116 costs rose slightly due to new North America site go-live.
capex / expansion: Asset-light strategy maintained; no heavy fixed asset capex; investments limited to warehouse tech, robotics, and unified logistics platform (patent applied); Lease optimization (short/medium term vs long term) reduced interest costs YoY.
capital allocation: Priority allocation to ISCS growth initiatives; Working capital tightly managed (Rs 243 cr operating cash flow FY26); Net debt low (~Rs 350-370 cr) with strong AA rating; Inorganic growth via tuck-in acquisitions (e.g., Swamy & Sons).
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical disruptions affecting global trade lanes (West Asia hotspot); Volatility in global freight rates impacting GFS pricing; Customer churn in GFS segment; Execution risk in integrating new acquisitions and entering regulated sectors (Defense).
management quality / tone: Highly confident and bullish on FY27; Emphasis on 'spectacular finish' and 'unprecedented growth'; Strategic focus on deepening Fortune 500 relationships and tech-led differentiation; Cautious only on GFS pricing volatility.
non-obvious takeaways: Europe business has structurally turned around contributing to margin expansion; Average contract length is highly sticky (4+ years India, 7.5 years Europe); US strategy is deliberately narrow (Auto/Industrial) to mine large accounts rather than broaden verticals too quickly; Integrated Final Mile (IFM) sub-segment has completed corrective actions and is now on a strong profitability path.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

Operations are organised into two segments: Integrated Supply Chain Solutions (ISCS) and Global Forwarding Solutions (GFS).
